angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 563,517 km at 95.97 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.4195 +/- 0.0096 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 95.97 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.81 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1758 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 563,517 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.88 +/- 0.11 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1758 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5169 +/- 122 K from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1758 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1758 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1758.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.566, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
